newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oct/Dec soybean crush at record high-Oil World.
newsitem.headline: Oct/Dec soybean crush at record high-Oil World.

text.p: World soybean crushings in October/December 1996 were at a record high of 29.9 million tonnes, compared with 29.6 million one year earlier and 27.5 million two years earlier, the independent Oil World newsletter said.

It said the United States, Europe, Canada, Mexico and some Asian countries increased their soybean processing because of strong demand and in response to reduced soybean supplies in Latin America and rapeseed crop shortfalls elsewhere.
U.S. soybean crushings in the three months were pegged at 10.8 million tonnes and those in the EU at 4.0 million -- both up by eight percent from the same 1995 period.
The EU in October/December crushed 17 percent more sunseed than a year earlier at 1.74 million and 500,000 tonnes less rapeseed at 1.61 million, Oil World also noted.
Combined Argentine and Brazilian crushings dropped by 12 percent to 6.9 million tonnes in the three months while Canada boosted soybean crushings by nearly 25 percent to 400,000 tonnes.

The publication also forecast the U.S. soybean crush in January/March 1997 at 10.2 million tonnes, up by 700,000 tonnes from the first quarter of 1996, but said it should slow after that in response to tight availability.
